title: South Sudan
capsule: South Sudan became the world's newest internationally recognized state on 9 July 2011 following a January 2011 independence referendum in which 98.83% voted to secede from Sudan, the culmination of the Second Sudanese Civil War (1983–2005) that killed approximately two million people. The country immediately faced severe structural challenges: it controls roughly 75% of former Sudan's oil reserves but landlocked dependence on Sudanese pipelines for export created immediate revenue crises. Civil war erupted in December 2013 between forces loyal to President Salva Kiir and former vice president Riek Machar, producing one of the world's worst humanitarian disasters with hundreds of thousands killed and millions displaced before successive peace agreements from 2015 onward.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. South Sudan's international boundaries are defined by the 1956 Anglo-Egyptian Sudan colonial demarcation, though the Abyei region boundary with Sudan and portions of the South Sudan–Uganda–Kenya border remain disputed or incompletely demarcated.
